paragraphs.source_en: The archaeological record from the Central Sahara gives information about the settlement of the pastoralists and their material culture. Pastoral pottery was different from that of the hunters since it was more thinwalled and with different decoration which no longer covered the whole surface of containers. In the lithic industry microliths were replaced by tools of a much lower technological sophistication, represented mainly by rough blades (Barich 2002). The research (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996b) revealed numerous open air sites, related to the earliest Pastoral phase from about 7,500 to 6,500 BP. These sites, real villages, were detected in the lowlands east of the Acacus, along the shores of ancient lakes.

units.source_en: The archaeological record from the Central Sahara gives information about the settlement of the pastoralists and their material culture.
Pastoral pottery was different from that of the hunters since it was more thinwalled and with different decoration which no longer covered the whole surface of containers.
In the lithic industry microliths were replaced by tools of a much lower technological sophistication, represented mainly by rough blades (Barich 2002).
The research (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996b) revealed numerous open air sites, related to the earliest Pastoral phase from about 7,500 to 6,500 BP.
These sites, real villages, were detected in the lowlands east of the Acacus, along the shores of ancient lakes.

paragraphs.source_en: Considering the abundance of cattle remains there, these sites could represent the principal areas of occupation from which groups would seasonally move in search of pasture (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996b).

units.source_en: Considering the abundance of cattle remains there, these sites could represent the principal areas of occupation from which groups would seasonally move in search of pasture (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996b).

paragraphs.source_en: The places which provided grass during dry periods were located in the neighbouring Acacus Mountains, which were also frequented by the hunter-gatherers. The research in the Acacus (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996a) showed that whereas in the Epipalaeolithic period sites in the lowlands were quite abundant, in the later Mesolithic period they were almost abandoned due to the increasing aridity, so that the huntergatherers were concentrated exclusively in the mountains. During the Pastoral phase the climate was again wetter but with probably more short arid phases in the lowlands, forcing people to migrate seasonally from the lowlands into mountains. Thus, in some periods of the year the herders and the foragers had to share the same territory.

paragraphs.source_en: The excavated shelters revealed that the Epipalaeolithic and Mesolithic hunter-gatherer occupation was followed by the Pastoral phase after 7,500 BP. What happened then to the hunters? The shelters are located in the lowest part of the wadies which were the easiest places to access with herds. Shelters in the upper terraces of wadies were not excavated; these places were difficult to access for animals but not for people, and so they would have been suitable for the hunters. With such a division of the territory the coexistence of pastoralists with hunters may have been possible.
